description: The default impl returns Ok(()) (skip). Any custom RevocationChecker implementation that doesn't override check_revocation_against_anchor silently skips the anchor-issued cert revocation check with no compile error. The docs explain the default but a busy developer adding a CRL-or-OCSP checker will test check_revocation and miss check_revocation_against_anchor entirely. The concrete consequence: a revoked intermediate CA issued directly by the trust anchor passes revocation checking in verify_chain. Consider whether this should be a required method (breaking) or add a #[must_override] doc note and integration test that verifies an overriding implementation.
title: RevocationChecker::check_revocation_against_anchor default Ok(()) is a silent security gap for custom impls
